basis: Renal magnesium wasting defines the electrolyte disorder; intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures occurred in 2/2 patients.
Placental neoplasm; placental and reproductive tissues fall outside the 13 axes.
Germ cell tumor arising in the lung.
Neuroblastic tumor arising from sympathetic nervous tissue; no additional organ involvement established across the group.
Wilms tumor arising in the kidney, without nuclear anaplasia.
Developmental brain malformations and intellectual disability define the tubulinopathy; skin creases characterize one subtype and are not established across most patients.
Cortical malformations and intellectual disability define CK syndrome; strabismus and kyphoscoliosis each occur in 80-99%. Dental crowding alone does not establish oral damage.
Bartter type 4B combines renal salt wasting, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and characteristic sensorineural deafness.
Microphthalmia, retinal degeneration and refractive abnormalities define ocular disease; dental anomalies are a defining component.
Myopathy with respiratory failure 2/2, liver injury 2/2, polymicrogyria 1/2; LV hypertrophy and deafness (1/2 each) omitted at cap. Respiratory failure reflects muscle dysfunction.
Corneal ulceration directly damages the eye; ring morphology alone does not establish an infectious or immune cause.
Mitochondrial complex I disorder with lactic acidosis; neurologic involvement includes infantile spasms in 1/3 and abnormal brain MRI. Optic atrophy frequency is unspecified.
Malignant neoplasm affecting the kidney in childhood.
Skin/hair hypopigmentation defines GS; immunodeficiency occurs in 30-79%. Cytopenias commonly reflect separately diagnosed HLH; neurologic and hepatic damage are mostly <30%.
Cerebrovascular infarction causes structural brain injury even when clinically silent.
Carcinoma arises at the hepatopancreatic ampulla, involving the duodenal/biliary junction; classified under both ampullary and extrahepatic bile duct carcinomas.
Cancer involving the femur directly occupies and damages bone.
Carcinoma in situ involving rectal epithelium.
Absent right ventricular myocardium causes ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias and heart failure; pleural effusion occurs in fewer than 30%.
Bacterial infection usually damages nasal, pharyngeal and oral mucosa through pseudomembranous inflammation. Myocarditis and neuropathy are minority, separately diagnosed complications.
Sacral and anorectal malformations define the triad; anterior sacral meningocele occurs in 30-79% as a major presacral lesion. Renal anomalies and tethered cord are <30%.
Lysosomal glycoprotein storage disorder. Splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ dysfunction; gout frequency and attributable joint damage are unspecified.
Secondary cutaneous mucin deposition defines this skin disorder; a lymphoma subtype does not establish lymphoma across the umbrella.
Congenital atrial septal defect with characteristic atrioventricular conduction abnormalities; manifestations remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia defines disease; arthrogryposis, esotropia and astigmatism each occur in 2/6. Cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic; cardiac lesions are <30%.
